svg.text: flat cut-outs living in a subsector, drawn after its walls, clipped by the same span list, and closing it behind themselves
THE GREEN ARMOUR · POSE (-104,-3232,128) · THE SPAN SET AS REAL TRAPEZIA, BEFORE AND AFTER THE OBJECT
the object is drawn AFTER its subsector's walls, and it closes columns like a wall does — only on its BOT side
columns 101→155 now bounded by its top edge
the aperture reaches the floor: one wide trapezium
the billboard is not in the list yet; it is about to put itself there
10 thin trapezia now trace the armour's top edge
Every one is BOT side: a cut-out blocks what is below its
top edge and nothing above it. Only the top edge tightens.
The template puts the 20 outline lines FIRST, drawn through
the plain clipper; a control entry then arms the walker and
the 10 top-edge lines follow, each drawing and applying in one
walk. Drawn first, the outline is never clipped by its own edge.
Probe 1, before any art: span_has_gap over [101,156).
A column is still open, so the slot is built at all;
all closed would retire it before a single line.
Probe 2, after the art ladders: box [101,155]x[76,106]
on screen, and every span across it holds it inside
[IT,IB] with no gap: PASSED, so the 20 outline lines
skip the clipper and go straight to the plotter.
ONE BILLBOARD, STEP BY STEP · EVERY COUNT FROM THIS FRAME
LEVEL OF DETAIL · BOTH TIERS OF EVERY KIND AT ONE HEIGHT AND ONE PIXEL SCALE · THE SHAPE IS SWAPPED, NOT SCALED
objects are 9.9% of the render suite · six slots a subsector · nearest first · probe 1 can retire a whole slot, probe 2 can free it from the clipper · only the top edge tightens
